newsitem.title: CHINA: Hainan set for landmark China airline listing.
newsitem.headline: Hainan set for landmark China airline listing.

text.p: Hainan Airlines is set to become the first Chinese airline to issue shares publicly, with a listing of foreign currency B shares on the Shanghai stock market within this year, the company said on Friday.
Brokers said that there would be strong interest in the first listing from China's booming aviation sector but added the company was small and the Shanghai B market short of liquidity.

Hainan Airlines has received regulatory approval for the issue, the China Securities newspaper said on Friday. The company aims to list 71 million shares on the Shanghai bourse by the end of 1996 and will use the proceeds to acquire new planes and related equipment, a company official said.
The issue price has not been decided, she said.
The company is 25 percent owned by American Aviation Investment, a fund partially controlled by U.S. financier George Soros, making it the first Chinese airline to become a joint venture company.

Dominic Yee, associate director in Shanghai of W.I. Carr, the international coordinator for the issue, said that it was a rare opportunity to get into China's aviation industry, a fast growing sector.

"The size of the issue is too small for a Hong Kong listing," he said. "The company has a hub in Ningbo (south of Shanghai) and in future hopes to operate international routes, so Shanghai makes more sense than Shenzhen."
Shenzhen is home to China's other stock market.

Beijing has selected two airlines, China Eastern and China Southern, for an overseas stock listing but brokers said that neither was likely this year. That would make Hainan the first airline to issue shares publicly.
Brokers welcomed the news. "The aviation concept is very good and investors will want exposure to this sector in China," one Chinese broker said.

"But, while the overall concept is good, we will have to look closely at the airline," he said. "It is small, with no international routes. Margins are lower on domestic routes and competition very fierce."
The airline operates more than 30 domestic routes and aims to launch overseas services in 1997, the company official said.
"The fact that it is the first airline stock should create interest," said one foreign broker.
"But liquidity is always a negative factor for the B market," he said. "It is a problem with the Shanghai market, not with the company itself."
While Shanghai's domestic A share market has been on a bull run this year, the B share market has been in a long-term slump, with turnover of just several million dollars a day.
Hainan Airlines posted turnover of 480 million yuan ($57.8 million) in 1995, the company official said but declined to give a forecast for 1996.
In August, a company official said 1995 net earnings were 81 million yuan, down from 87 million in 1994.
